gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans draws every line like it was traced along a ruler. Eight Bit Dragon, with its widely spaced letters and mild stroke variation, gives that tube-like constant line a lively, towering foil.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-yaldevi: Yaldevi reads clean, with an e whose eye opens clearly rightward. Eight Bit Dragon does swagger best, striding across spaced-out letters, while Yaldevi's outsized lowercase does the quiet, steady talking.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-aldrich: Aldrich reads like tracing a single thick thread, with its x-height close to the capitals and round letters cupped rather than clenched. Electroharmonix breaks words into spaced single letters, loud against that tidy line.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-alexandria: Alexandria reads clean and tall-bodied, with generous c terminals and short stems above and below that keep lines moving. Under Electroharmonix, a full page of this would glide on.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-amiko: Amiko brings lowercase strokes as tall as a thick crayon mark, with terminals that point outward like a pair of tongs. Electroharmonix shouts in split letters, and that sturdy body keeps its footing.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-anek-bangl: Loud meets friendly: Electroharmonix splits words into single letters while Anek Bangla keeps its s curves wide and barely curled. Its short ascender reach keeps the body low-key beside the heading's flair.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-anek-devan: Striking and spaced out, Electroharmonix breaks each word into single letters with open-handed curves. Anek Devanagari counters with distinctly open letter mouths and a tall middle zone that keep the page grounded.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-anek-gujar: Electroharmonix breaks each word into single letters, with open-handed curves in every round character. And Anek Gujarati lets its lowercase rival the capitals, with a gaping c opening to match.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-anek-gurmu: Clean counters fill every small letter of Anek Gurmukhi, and its round characters open their hands just as the heading's do. Electroharmonix spaces its letters apart while the body fills in quietly.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-anek-kanna: Electroharmonix breaks every word into lone, spaced-out letters. Anek Kannada steadies the page, its high, squared-off x-height plus terminals stopping far from the stem making long paragraphs move along smoothly.
